summary.title: MQTT broker from scratch #5 - Topic abstraction
summary.one_liner: You learn how MQTT topics with / separators and # and + wildcards map onto a trie, and how to implement a trie in C using sorted linked-list children.
takeaways: MQTT topics are UTF-8 strings up to 65535 bytes, split by '/', with '#' (multilevel) and '+' (single level) wildcards for subscriptions.
A trie stores keys by prefix, giving O(m) worst-case insert and lookup, where m is the key length, and enabling prefix range scans useful for wildcard matching.
A trie with a fixed array of ALPHABET_SIZE pointers per node wastes a lot of memory, since most pointers stay NULL.
Three alternatives to reduce waste are a single vector with child indexes, nodes sized by child count, and sorted singly-linked child lists (the approach chosen here).
The article provides a C implementation in trie.h and trie.c with insert, find, delete, prefix delete and prefix map functions.
summary.summary: The author recaps MQTT topic rules, including the / level separator and the # and + wildcards, and explains why a trie suits storing topics. The post walks through the memory cost of a fixed-array trie node, compares three mitigation strategies, and picks a sorted linked-list child structure. It then presents the C header and implementation (trie.h and trie.c) covering insertion, lookup, recursive deletion, prefix deletion and prefix mapping. The page closes with the planned project layout and points to Part 6 on server-side handlers.
